rules.title: Password spraying / brute force (many failed logons)
rules.description: A burst of failed logons. Many accounts from one source suggests spraying; one account many times suggests brute force.
rules.recommendation: Identify the source IP/host, block it, and confirm no success (4624) followed. Enforce lockout and MFA.

rules.title: Successful logon after repeated failures (likely cracked)
rules.description: An account that failed to log on many times then succeeded from the same source — the hallmark of a guessed or sprayed password.
rules.recommendation: Reset the account password, review what the session did, and check the source host.

rules.title: Sensitive privileges assigned at logon (admin-equivalent)
rules.description: A logon was granted sensitive privileges (effectively admin). Normal for admins and services; useful as timeline context.
rules.recommendation: Correlate with the matching 4624 and confirm the account is meant to have these rights.

rules.title: Security event log cleared
rules.description: The Security log was cleared. Attackers do this to destroy evidence; it is almost never part of normal operations.
rules.recommendation: Find who cleared it and when, and recover logs from your SIEM or forwarded copies.

rules.title: System/application event log cleared
rules.recommendation: Confirm whether this was a sanctioned maintenance action.

rules.title: New service installed
rules.description: A new Windows service was installed whose program looks like a script interpreter or sits in a user-writable path — common for persistence and lateral movement (PsExec-style).
rules.recommendation: Inspect the service's binary path and signature; remove it if not legitimate.

rules.title: Scheduled task created
rules.description: A scheduled task was created that runs a script host or a user-folder program.
rules.recommendation: Review the task action and trigger; remove it if unexpected.

rules.title: Suspicious process creation (command-line rules)
rules.description: Process-creation events are run through the full living-off-the-land rule set, so historical 4688 logs are analyzed the same way as live processes.
rules.recommendation: See the matched command-line rule for specifics.

rules.title: Suspicious PowerShell script block
rules.description: Recorded PowerShell script blocks are scanned with the command-line rules, catching encoded commands, download cradles, AMSI bypasses and reflective loading.
rules.recommendation: See the matched rule; recover the full script block for analysis.

rules.title: PowerShell logging was reduced or disabled
rules.description: A script tried to turn off PowerShell history or script-block logging — covering tracks.
rules.recommendation: Treat subsequent PowerShell activity as under-logged; pull any history that remains.

rules.title: New user account created
rules.description: A new account was created. Normal in managed environments; suspicious on a workstation or outside a change window.
rules.recommendation: Confirm the account is expected and who created it.

rules.title: Member added to a privileged local group
rules.description: An account was added to local Administrators or Remote Desktop Users.
rules.recommendation: Verify authorization; remove and investigate if not.

rules.title: Member added to a privileged domain group
rules.description: An account was added to a highly privileged domain group — a major escalation if unexpected.
rules.recommendation: Confirm with your change process immediately; this is a common post-compromise action.

rules.title: Defender protection events
rules.description: Microsoft Defender reported being disabled, modified or that it detected malware. Protection changes near other suspicious activity are a red flag.
rules.recommendation: Check what changed, re-enable protection, and review detections.

rules.title: Interactive/RDP logon from an external address
rules.description: An interactive or remote-desktop logon came from a public IP address. Direct RDP from the internet is a common intrusion vector.
rules.recommendation: Confirm the source is expected; restrict RDP exposure and require MFA/VPN.
